record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Let E be a non-normable separable Frechet space, and let L(E) denote its continuous linear operators. Does there exist an infinite-dimensional linear subspace A of L(E) such that every nonzero operator T in A is hypercyclic, meaning that some vector has dense orbit {T^n x : n in N}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a separable, non-normable Fréchet space over the complex numbers, and let $L(E)$ denote the algebra of continuous linear operators $T : E \to E$. An operator $T \in L(E)$ is said to be hypercyclic if there exists a vector $x \in E$ whose orbit $\{T^n x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is dense in $E$. 

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional linear subspace $\mathcal{A} \subseteq L(E)$ such that every nonzero operator $T \in \mathcal{A}$ is hypercyclic?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal a closely related, well-studied notion of "hypercyclic subspaces" (infinite-dimensional closed subspaces of E consisting, except for zero, of hypercyclic vectors for a single operator), which is now known to exist for every infinite-dimensional separable Fréchet space. However, the present problem asks for an infinite-dimensional linear subspace of the operator space L(E) all of whose nonzero elements are hypercyclic operators — a different question. No source located confirms a resolution of this specific question for non-normable separable Fréchet spaces, so the current status is treated as unknown (likely still open).

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic Subspaces on Fréchet Spaces Without Continuous Norm
status_evidence.snippet: Each infinite-dimensional separable Fréchet space supports a mixing operator with a hypercyclic subspace.
status_evidence.claim: Related results about hypercyclic subspaces of vectors (not of operators) are now known on all separable Fréchet spaces.

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic Operators on Non-normable Fréchet Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every infinite dimensional separable non-normable Fréchet space admits a continuous hypercyclic operator.
status_evidence.claim: Hypercyclic operators exist on every separable non-normable Fréchet space, providing the setting of the question.

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic subspaces for Fréchet space operators
status_evidence.snippet: Every infinite-dimensional separable Fréchet space admitting a continuous norm supports an operator for which there is an infinite-dimensional closed subspace consisting, except for zero, of hypercyclic vectors.
status_evidence.claim: The literature addresses hypercyclic subspaces of vectors, but the question about subspaces inside L(E) is not addressed by the located sources.
